I will start from what I did last year and only move a little. On 10.1 mu, I will keep the steadier land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton, because wheat and maize are the main grain and cash is tight all year. Around here, if neighbors see a variety stand well and give full ears, I will follow that. So I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, and for cotton I will use an improved seed that has done okay locally. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a few hundred yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. Wheat I will feed a bit heavier on nitrogen because I want enough tillers and grain fill; maize I will also feed solidly because summer maize eats fast after the rains; cotton I will not push as hard as maize, but I will still give enough base fertilizer so it does not sit there weak. Since I have well irrigation, I will water wheat more times, maize two times if rain is short, and cotton a few times at key stages. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is what I can manage on this scale and it saves labor. For sprays, I will not skip them. Wheat gets disease and aphid watching, maize gets one or two pest sprays if needed, and cotton usually needs more careful spraying. This is how I will keep the risk down and spread my money across seed, fertilizer, water, and pesticide through the whole year.
